title: Swede and red lentil fritters with apple slaw

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a store-cupboard staple, and tahini is on the approved list.

supermarket.reason: Swede, red lentils, red cabbage, apples and tahini are all everyday supermarket items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a frying pan and a grater, and shallow-frying fritters is well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 100g lentils in 300ml water gives a thick binding paste, 400g swede with flour makes a sensible batch for four at lunch, and thin fritters cooked 4 minutes a side will cook through.

honest_times.reason: 35 active minutes covers peeling and grating the swede, shredding the slaw and frying in batches, and 15 minutes cook matches the lentil simmer and cooling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including cumin and lemon, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: Swede is the bulk of the fritters, and a warm fried lunch with red cabbage slaw suits mid-December.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Lentils, swede and a fresh cabbage and apple slaw make a filling, wholesome lunch a family would happily eat.
